# You are a coding agent on slop.computer (local test server)

slop.computer hosts **artifacts**: a *page* is a folder with index.html (+ css/js), a *data*
artifact is a folder of records (Markdown posts with front matter, JSON files, and plain files
such as images). Every push makes a new numbered **version**; `main` follows the newest push.
**Routes** map paths on the site host (site.localhost:18120) to a page; a route follows main
unless pinned to a version. The Workshop is at http://localhost:18120.

This server holds an import of the real francois catalog (slop.boutique), in project `francois`:

- `francois-catalog` (data): one JSON record per catalog artifact, file `<id>.json`. Fields:
  title, description, tags, visibility, featured, sortOrder, earlyAccessUntil, demoEnabled,
  launchMode, creators (slugs), body (Markdown), cover {id, src, type, width, height, alt},
  gallery [same shape], releases [{version, n, state, freeSample, capabilities, publishedAt,
  changelog}], latest (version string), page (the page artifact holding the releases, if any),
  francoisId.
- `francois-media` (data): image files `files/<id>.<ext>`; in `window.slop.data` they are
  records with `file: true` and a `src` URL. `cover.src` and `gallery[].src` already point there.
- `francois-creators` (data): `<slug>.json` {name, bio, links, avatar}.
- One page artifact per catalog artifact that has releases (e.g. `weft`, `vitrine`): its
  versions are the francois releases, `index.html` is the release HTML (or a placeholder page
  when the HTML was not importable).

The `slop` CLI is on your PATH and already logged in. Useful commands:

    slop artifacts list                         # every artifact, its kind, project, main version
    slop pull <artifact> [dir]                  # write the main version into dir
    slop push <dir> -m "what changed"           # new version from the folder
    slop push <dir> -a <name> -m "first" --project <project> --title "Title"   # a NEW page
    slop route list                             # routes on the site host
    slop route set /path <artifact>             # route a path to a page (follows main)
    slop route set /journal/:slug journal-post --record 'posts/{slug}.md' --bind posts=journal

A page reads data by naming it in its slop.json: {"reads": {"catalog": "francois-catalog"}}; the
page then gets `window.slop.data.catalog.list()` (a Promise of records) and, under a route with
--record, `window.slop.record` (the record's path) and `window.slop.route.params`.
Look at the existing `journal-index` and `journal-post` pages (project lab-site): pull them to see
how a list page and a per-record page are built, and reuse their `boutique.css`.

Rules:
- Keep pages small and self-contained: no external network requests, no build step, no CDN.
- Always push with a clear -m message. Never delete other people's routes.
- Check what you build: curl -s http://site.localhost:18120/<path> | head -60

# Storefront on slop — what was hard Working directory: `.../scratchpad/agents-import/manuel/work` Artifacts: `storefront` (v2), `storefront-entry` (v2), project `francois`. Routes I ended up with: ``` / storefront main /apps/:id storefront-entry main --record '{id}.json' --bind catalog=francois-catalog /r/ @ pinned to the record's latest release (100 routes) /lab-home front-page (old "/" kept reachable) /experiments/:slug app-page (old /apps/:slug kept reachable) ``` Everything below is something slop did that cost time, forced a workaround, or made the obvious solution impossible. --- ## 1. Data-file URLs are dead until a routed page `reads` the artifact `francois-catalog` gives every cover/gallery/body image a URL like ``` /_d/francois-media/main/files/med_4947accd98487d2a911d34a6.png ``` and `window.slop.data.media` records carry `src: "/_d/francois-media/1/files/…"`. Both returned **404 `Nothing is routed here.`** at the start of the session. I tried `/_d/`, `/_v/`, `/_f/`, `/files/`, `/_slop/d/…`, the sandbox host, `Host:` overrides, `Referer`/`Origin` headers — all 404. What actually enabled them was unrelated: I pushed a throwaway page `probe-media` with ```json {"reads": {"media": "francois-media", "catalog": "francois-catalog"}} ``` and routed it at `/probe`. Immediately after that, the same URLs were 200: ``` /_d/francois-media/main/index.json 404 -> 200 (80179 B) /_d/francois-catalog/main/aasd.json 404 -> 200 /_d/francois-media-2/main/files/med_907a9d9b….png 404 (still) ``` Adding `francois-media-2`, `-3` and `francois-creators` to the same `reads` map made those reachable too. So: **a data artifact's files are only served publicly if some routed page declares the read.** Nothing in `slop --help`, `slop help push`, or the route table says this; the generated `src` values are lies until then. What I did instead: both pages declare all three media artifacts (`media`, `media2`, `media3`) even though they only need the URLs, and I never call `slop.data.media.list()`. Practical consequence: every page now carries the 692 media records in its boot payload (see §2). ## 2. `reads` is page-wide, so an entry page ships the whole catalogue `GET /apps/weft` is **679 KB**, of which **667 KB** is the injected `#slop-boot` JSON: ``` catalog: 104 records (full Markdown bodies, galleries, release arrays) media: 304 media2: 360 media3: 28 (file records) ``` There is no per-route or per-record projection, no field selection, and no server-side filtering: `slop.data.catalog.list()` returns every record including 5 `hidden` ones and I filter `visibility === "listed"` in JS. The list page needs titles and covers, but gets all bodies. The record page needs one record, but gets 105, plus three media indexes because of §1. What I did instead: nothing clever — accepted the payload, because the alternative (duplicating the images into the page artifact) is worse; see §3. ## 3. There is no way to expose a folder of data files except via `reads` The obvious fix for §1 would be to serve `francois-media` from a route. Routes refuse: ``` $ slop route set /media francois-media invalid_request: francois-media is a data artifact; routes serve pages ``` Copying the images into the page artifact is the only route-free option. Covers alone are **77 MB** across 96 files; the three media artifacts are **310 MB** of galleries and screenshots. A push that size is not a working loop, and `slop push` has no partial upload for a page. What I did instead: declared the `reads` (§1), used `cover.src` verbatim, rewrote only the absolute origin (`https://slop.boutique/_d/…` → `/_d/…`) so no request leaves the host, and added a monogram fallback for the 6 listed records with no cover (`note-g`, `loom-hours`, `brand-crystal`, `porous-forge`, …). ## 4. Page assets live at an undocumented `/_v/` path with different rules `boutique.css` is a file inside the page artifact. To find how it is served I had to guess: `/_d/about/3/boutique.css` → 404; `/_v/about/3/boutique.css` → **200**. Rules I inferred by probing: | URL | result | | --- | --- | | `/_v/about/3/boutique.css` | 200 | | `/_v/about/main/boutique.css` | 404 (numeric version only) | | `/_v/weft/1/index.html` before `weft` was routed | 404 | | `/_v/weft/1/index.html` after `slop route set /r/weft weft` | 200 | | `/_v/francois-media/1/files/x.png` (data artifact) | 404 | | `/_v/about/3/slop.json` | 404 (config is private) | So `/_v/` is for **routed page artifacts only**, numeric versions only. Nothing in the docs mentions `/_v/`; the only reason I found it is that `/_d/` was failing and I brute-forced path prefixes. What I did instead: used relative ``, which works (see §5), and copied `boutique.css` into both page folders. ## 5.
